source.title: Improving the Trainability of Deep Neural Networks through Layerwise Batch-Entropy Regularization
source.authors: David Peer; Bart Keulen; Sebastian Stabinger; J. Piater; A. Rodríguez-Sánchez

record.tranche_reason: Tests deep-network trainability with a different intervention, layerwise batch-entropy regularization, and reports outcomes for very deep networks without skip connections.
record.gate_note: The study reports CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 residual-network test accuracies, but not their training classification errors. Its 500-layer training curves are figure-only; the text states the models without batch-entropy regularization were not trainable.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates batch-entropy regularization and related trainability failures, but does not test a stated claim version. Its deep CNN experiment uses MNIST without batch normalization and lacks a shallower or matched identity-shortcut comparator. Test accuracy alone does not establish the training-error comparisons in V1 or V3. Initialization effects, learning-rate stability thresholds, and batch-normalization acceleration are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that layerwise batch-entropy regularization can make initially untrainable networks trainable, including 500-layer plain fully connected and convolutional networks, and can improve performance across several architectures and tasks. They also argue that positive batch-entropy at every layer is necessary for successful gradient-based optimization.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a layerwise batch-entropy regularization term to the loss; this is not the original shortcut, initialization, learning-rate, or batch-normalization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Trainability of the 500-layer FNN differed across the tested normalization methods versus batch-entropy regularization; the text gives test accuracy for those conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch-entropy regularization enables 500-layer MNIST networks to learn, reaching 95.2% FNN and 99.2% CNN test accuracy; the authors report failure without the regularizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise batch-entropy regularization can enable learning in very deep plain MNIST networks under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The tested normalization methods leave 500-layer MNIST fully connected networks near chance test accuracy, despite learning-rate and seed selection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested normalization recipes are insufficient to train these 500-layer fully connected networks successfully.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports 11.35% test accuracy without regularization at depths 30–50, versus 92.84–93.51% with regularization; shallower fully connected networks learn without it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-related learning failure in these MNIST fully connected networks can be alleviated by batch-entropy regularization.

record.problems: The deep vanilla network evidence is on MNIST, not CIFAR; the 500-layer training curves are figures, and the paper does not give their training-error values in text. Table 5 reports only the best test accuracy for each normalization method, without uncertainty.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, stopping time, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depths in plain batch-normalized CNNs, its prevention by matched identity shortcuts, longer training, and the named initialization exceptions.
Effects of initialization choices on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V3 verdicts: successful learning with an additional regularizer does not qualify the specific V3 comparison, and failed fully connected networks do not support it. The figure curves are unavailable as readable numerical data in the supplied text. No missing result directly tests a stated version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size or training duration on that error.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
The study does not compare plain networks with matched identity-shortcut networks, test ImageNet training error, or evaluate the special initializations and Fixup recipe named in this version.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above the stability threshold, loss curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or tolerates higher learning rates on the listed tasks, and whether Fixup matches its performance.

rows.subject: 500-layer fully connected network (FNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with batch-entropy regularization; authors report test accuracy.
rows.note: Authors say this shows the network can be trained; no matching numerical no-regularizer value is given in text.
rows.check: The 95.2% test accuracy measures regularized fully connected network performance on MNIST, whereas V3 specifies training-error degradation in convolutional networks.

rows.subject: 500-layer convolutional neural network (CNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with batch-entropy regularization, without pooling, skip connections, or other normalization; authors report test accuracy.
rows.note: The study does not provide a numeric test-accuracy baseline without batch-entropy regularization.
rows.check: The 99.2% test accuracy establishes successful learning with the proposed regularizer, but provides no training-error comparison across depths or against identity shortcuts. The CNN has no batch normalization and uses MNIST.

rows.subject: 500-layer fully connected network (FNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without batch-entropy regularization using batch normalization; best-performing learning rate and seed reported.
rows.note: The authors state they were unable to train a 500-layer vanilla FNN with any tested normalization method.
rows.check: Value is 11.74% test accuracy. Failure of a 500-layer ReLU fully connected network does not measure V3's convolutional depth comparison or V6's training-speed and learning-rate advantages. Appendix F specifies 500 training epochs; Table 5 selects the best test accuracy across learning rates and seeds.

rows.subject: 500-layer fully connected network (FNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without batch-entropy regularization using layer normalization; best-performing learning rate and seed reported.
rows.note: The authors state they were unable to train a 500-layer vanilla FNN with any tested normalization method.
rows.check: Value is 11.35% test accuracy. Layer-normalized fully connected network trainability does not measure any version. Appendix F specifies 500 epochs and reports the best test accuracy across learning rates and seeds.

rows.subject: 500-layer fully connected network (FNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without batch-entropy regularization using self-normalizing neural networks with SELU activation; best-performing learning rate and seed reported.
rows.note: The authors state they were unable to train a 500-layer vanilla FNN with any tested normalization method.
rows.check: Value is 11.35% test accuracy. A self-normalizing SELU fully connected network does not test the convolutional depth comparison or an initialization comparison. Appendix F specifies 500 epochs and reports the best test accuracy across learning rates and seeds.

rows.subject: 500-layer fully connected network (FNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without batch-entropy regularization using weight normalization; best-performing learning rate and seed reported.
rows.note: The authors state they were unable to train a 500-layer vanilla FNN with any tested normalization method.
rows.check: Value is 11.35% test accuracy. Weight-normalized fully connected network trainability does not measure any version. Appendix F specifies 500 epochs and reports the best test accuracy across learning rates and seeds.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 500-layer vanilla networks on MNIST with batch-entropy regularization
reader_labels.reason: The reported test accuracies show that very deep networks without skip connections can be trained under this added regularizer (R1, R2); this study does not test identity shortcuts against matched plain networks.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 500-layer fully connected networks on MNIST with the tested normalization methods
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that normalization methods did not make the 500-layer FNN trainable; the reported test accuracies were 11.74 or 11.35 (R3–R6).
